question_text: According to the course material, an organisation is a group of people bound together to provide unity of action for the achievement of:
explanation: An organisation is a group of people bound together to provide unity of action for a predetermined objective.

question_text: According to the course material, organisations can be classified into two broad headings:
explanation: Organisations are classified as formal and informal.

question_text: According to the course material, formal organisation is a planned pattern of group behaviour designed to achieve an objective, and reasons include establishing logical patterns of interrelationships, securing advantages of specialisation or division of labour, and:
option_a: coordinating activities of the component parts to realise the goals of the organisation
explanation: Massie and Douglas (1977) are cited: formal organisation coordinates component parts to realise organisational goals.

question_text: According to the course material, in Nigeria the problem of formal organisation is not so acute because of:
explanation: The problem of formal organisation is not so acute in Nigeria because of the nature of Nigerian businesses; small enterprises are easier to design than large ones.

question_text: According to the course material, communication is defined by Kazmier (1977) as the process of passing information and understanding from:
option_b: a machine to a rock only
option_d: only a notice board with no receiver
explanation: Kazmier: communication is passing information and understanding from one person to another.

question_text: According to the course material, it is a meaningful interaction among people where thoughts are transferred so that the meaning and value of such thoughts is the same in the minds of:
option_a: both the sender and the receiver
explanation: Meaning and value of the thoughts should be the same in the minds of both sender and receiver.

question_text: According to W.R. Spriegal, cited in the course material, most of the conflicts in business are not basic but are caused by misunderstood motives and:
explanation: Spriegal: most business conflicts are caused by misunderstood motives and ignorance of facts.

question_text: According to Peter Drucker (1954), cited in the course material, a manager does not handle people; he motivates, guides and organises people to accomplish their goals, and his effectiveness depends upon:
option_a: his ability to communicate well with the employees
explanation: Drucker: a manager's effectiveness depends on his ability to communicate well. Good communication is the foundation of sound management.

question_text: According to the course material, effective management is a function of effective communication; many operations have failed because of poor communication, misunderstood messages and:
explanation: Many operations have failed because of poor communication, misunderstood messages and unclear instructions.

question_text: According to the course material, directing and leading comprise the managerial function of guiding, overseeing and leading people; the primary element in this function is:
option_a: the human element and personal relationships
explanation: Directing and leading deal with the human element and personal relationships: leadership, motivation and communication.

question_text: According to Schneider (1975), cited in the course material, organisational climate refers to:
option_a: the entire internal environment of the organisation
option_d: only the colour of the roof
explanation: Schneider: organisational climate is the entire internal environment of the organisation.

question_text: According to Litwin and Stringer (1966), cited in the course material, climate characteristics include individual autonomy, how superiors communicate objectives and rules, types of behaviours rewarded, warmth and support from superiors, how conflict is managed, and:
option_a: the extent to which members are allowed to participate in decision making
explanation: Litwin and Stringer list autonomy, communication of objectives, rewards, warmth/support, conflict management, and participation in decisions.

question_text: According to the course material, the directing function is the action function that tests managerial capability; satisfactory performance depends partly on directional ability but primarily on:
explanation: If the environment is not conducive, directing alone cannot bring optimum results.

question_text: According to the course material, staffing is the traditional management function of attraction and selection of the best people, putting them on jobs where their talents can best be utilised, and retention through incentives, job training and:
explanation: Staffing: attract and select the best, place them well, retain them through incentives, training and job enrichment.

question_text: According to the course material, the staffing function is generally handled by the Personnel Department, concerned with planning, organising, directing and controlling of the procurement, development, compensation and integration of people for:
explanation: Personnel management integrates people into the system for organisational, individual and social goals.

question_text: According to the course material, recruitment is distinct from employment and selection: recruitment precedes selection and includes only finding, developing sources of prospective employees and attracting them to apply, whereas selection is:
option_a: finding out the most suitable candidate out of those attracted
explanation: Recruitment attracts a pool; selection finds the most suitable candidate from that pool.

question_text: According to Glueck (1978), cited in the course material, recruiting refers to those sets of activities an organisation uses to attract job candidates possessing the appropriate characteristics to help the organisation:
explanation: Glueck: recruiting attracts candidates with appropriate characteristics to help the organisation reach its objectives.

question_text: According to Byars and Rue (1984), cited in the course material, recruitment involves seeking and attracting a pool of people from which qualified candidates for job vacancies:
explanation: Byars and Rue: recruitment seeks and attracts a pool from which qualified candidates can be chosen.

question_text: According to the course material, subsystems of recruitment include finding and developing sources, developing suitable techniques to attract candidates, employing those techniques, and:
option_a: stimulating as many candidates as possible to apply
explanation: Four subsystems: find sources; develop attraction techniques; use them; stimulate as many candidates as possible to apply.

question_text: According to the course material, the selection unit also treats placement and:
explanation: After selection, the unit covers placement and induction of new employees.

question_text: According to the course material, all management theorists such as Fayol and Follet recognise organising as an important management function, and organisation is very fundamental to human nature because man is:
option_a: a social animal and shares relationship with his neighbours
explanation: Man is a social animal; organisation is central to sociology, psychology and even anthropology.

question_text: According to Prof. A. Dasgupta (1968), cited in the course material, two-way consulting between management and employees should cover knowledge of policies and objectives, results, plans, conditions of service, ways of improving efficiency, and:
option_a: all aspects of industrial safety, health and welfare
explanation: Dasgupta lists policies, results, plans, conditions of service, efficiency/productivity, and industrial safety, health and welfare.

question_text: According to the course material, the communication unit also treats the grapevine, barriers to effective communication, how to overcome those barriers, and:
explanation: Topics include grapevine, barriers, overcoming barriers, and guidelines for effective communication.

question_text: According to the course material, personnel policies change under social and legal pressure to increase the proportion of minority workers, affirmative action, and workers shifting their idea of success from good pay toward:
option_a: challenge, new opportunities, job enrichment and self-fulfilment
option_d: pay as the only remaining meaning of success
explanation: Success is increasingly measured by challenge, opportunity, job enrichment and self-fulfilment, not only good pay.

question_text: According to the course material, authority relationships treated under organising include functional authority and line authority, together with power and influence, sources of authority, limits of authority, and:
explanation: Organising covers functional and line authority, power and influence, sources and limits of authority, and levels in the organisation.
